sentences.text: These petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act seeking compensation for the death and injury caused in a road traffic accident.

As both the petitions were arising out of the same accident,
they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

2. The case of the petitioner is that on 29.05.2021 at about 10.00 a.m., when deceased Naveen Rajur(in MVC No.3813/21) and Dilip as a pillion rider (in MVC No.3814/21)were proceeding on the Motor cycle bearing No.KA- 18-X-2521 on Vedavathi bridge near VMP hotel, Hiriyur town,
Chitradurga, at that time, driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-52- A-5136 came in front of the motor cycle without any signal for taking turn hand or indicator signal, immediately show down and turned the lorry, due to which back portion of the lorry dashed against the motor cycle and Naveen Rajur and petitioner in MVC No.3814/21 sustained grievous injuries and Naveen Rajur died on the spot and he was shifted to Hiriyur govt., hospital wherein PM examination was conducted and handed over to the deadbody to the petitioners and petitioners shifted the deadbody to their residence by hiring vehicle and funeral and obsequies.
Petitioners spent more than Rs.2 lakhs.
Prior to the accident, Naveen Rajur was hale and healthy and was agriculturist and was earning Rs.25,000/-p.m. and maintain the family members.
Due to death of Naveen Rajur, petitioners lost the income and hence prays to award compensation of Rs.30 lakhs from the respondents.

3. The petitioner in MVC No.3814/21 sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to nearby government hospital, Hiriyur wherein after first aid treatment and referred to higher hospital in Mangala hospital at Hassan wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 30-5-2021 to 10-6-2021 and he is still continuing followup treatment and spent more than Rs.5 lakhs towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Due to accidental injuries petitioner suffering from disability and discomforts.

Further stated that pr6ior to the accident,
petitioner was hale and healthy and he was an agriculturist and student and was earning Rs.25,000/-p.m. due to accidental injuries, he lost the earning and earning capacity.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.

In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal and only respondent No.2 filed written statement.

5. Respondent No.2 filed objections in MVC No.3813/21 wherein contended that there is no declaration to the effect that no other claim petition is filed before any other forum/Tribunal on the same cause of action and on this score also petition is liable to be summarily dismissed and petition is bad for misjoinder of necessary parties.

The tribunal even otherwise is under statutory obligation under rule 235 of Karnataka motor vehicles Rules 1989 to send notice to owner/s and driver/s of the vehicles said to have been involved in an accident and call upon them to produce any evidence they may wish to tender on issue of negligence and as held by Apex court in case of Machindranath Kernath Kasar Vs D.S.Mylarappa and Ors on 29/4/2008(2008 ACJ page 1964) wherein it is held that driver is a necessary party to decide issue of negligence.

sentences.text: Principles of natural justice demand that persons must be given an opportunity to defend his/their action before held responsible or liable for his/their alleged action, omission or commission.
The respondent has violated section 158 (6) of MV Act.
The lorry bearing reg.No.KA-52-A-5136 was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate.
Hence prays to dismiss the petitions with costs.

6. The Tribunal in both case had framed the following issues:
ISSUES IN MVC No.3813 /2022 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Naveen Rajur S/o Late. Tirakappa died due to the grievous injury sustained by him in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-5136 on 29.05.202 at about 10.00 a.m. on Vedavathi bridge, near VP hotel Hiriyur town,
Chitradurga district and he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the respondents prove that accident has been take on place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle by the deceased Naveen Rajur S/o Late Tirakappa?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
5. What order or award?
ISSUES IN MVC No.3814/2021 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A- 5136 on 29-5-202 at about 10.00 a.m. on Vedavathi bridge, near VP hotel, Hiriyur town, Chitradurga district Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/

3 ? 
2. Whether the respondents prove that accident has been take on place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle by the deceased Naveen Rajur S/o Late Tirakappa?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom ?
4.

What order or award?
7.
The petitioner in MVC No.3813/2021 got examined herself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 11 and petitioner in MVC No.3814/2021 got examined himself as PW-2 and got marked Ex-P.12 to 18.
One Sharath S., Record Technician in Mangala Hospital, Hassan got examined as PW.3 and he got marked Ex.P.19 to P.23.
One Dr. K M Kumaraswamy in MVC 3814/2021 got examined as PW.4 and he got marked Ex.P.24 and P.25.

The respondent No.2 got examined its Manager G.Suresh as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1.
8.

The findings on the above issues in both cases are as follows :-
MVC NO.3813/2021 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative Issue No.4 : Partly in the affirmative Issue No.5 : As per final order for the following :-
and MVC No.3814/2021:-

REASONS 9. Issue No.1 in both cases : In order to prove the rash and negligence, petitioner in MVC No.3813/2021 Sakkavva Thirugappa Rajur, mother of deceased Naveen Raju got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.11 documents and petitioner in MVC No.3814/21 as PW-2.
On perusal of the records, soon after the accident Ningegowda S/o. Gangadharaiah lodged the complaint before the Hiriyur P.S. as per Ex.P.2.

Thereafter, Hiriyur police has filed FIR as per Ex.P.1 and after thorough investigation, filed charge sheet against deceased Naveen Rajur and also driver of the lorry for the offences punishable under Secs.279, 337 and 304-A of IPC and Sec. 196 of the IMV Act against the accused No.2 by holding that on 29.05.2021 at about 10.00 AM accused No.1-Naveen Rajur rode his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-X-2521 from Chithradurga towards Bengaluru in high speed, rash and negligent manner and at the same time, accused No.2 Praveen respondent No.1 in this case, who was the R.C.Owner and also driving the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-5136 in front of the motorcycle suddenly changed the lane from the middle lane to the last lane without giving any signal and putting indicator, as a result of which, accused No.1 i.e.,
deceased Naveen Rajur, who was driving the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-X-2521 hit to the Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/
4
back side of the lorry and due to the impact, accused No.1 deceased Naveen Rajur sustained grievous injuries and pillion rider-Dileepa Y.P. also sustained grievous injuries.

10. The learned counsel for petitioner has vehemently submitted that the respondent in collusion with the police have made to see that charge sheet is filed even against the deceased and that all the police documents except the charge sheet says that entire negligence is on the part of the offending vehicle No.2 and it is only in the charge sheet the allegation is made against the offending vehicle no.1.

The learned counsel further submitted that though charge sheet is against both the vehicles but primary document is to be looked into and charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to determine the negligence.
At this juncture this court has relied on unreported judgment in MFA No.201689/2016 (MV) Mahadevi & Ors., Vs. Shivaputra & Anr.

entities.text: MFA No.201689/2016 (MV) Mahadevi & Ors., Vs. Shivaputra & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein it was observed that "there is no law laid down in the said judgment of universal application that in all cases where charge sheets were filed,
unless Insurance Company challenges the same and obtains writ of mandamus, MACTs are required to act upon the same and proceed to come to a conclusion that the vehicles named as offending vehicles in the charge sheet, without any further proof, are to be taken as the motor vehicles involved in causing the accident, even in cases where evidence produced points to the contrary".

In the light of the contention taken by the petitioner to the aforesaid effect, if the materials placed on record is perused,
11.
Further during the investigation, it was found that accused No.1 owner of the motor cycle was riding the vehicle without insuring the motor cycle.
But mere accused No.1 deceased driving vehicle without insurance will not lead to inference that deceased was riding motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner.
Moreover petitioner is claiming compensation against insurance company or lorry.

12. On perusal of the sketch, the spot of accident is NH 4 highway road and both vehicles were moving in the same direction i.e., from Chitradurga towards Bangalore and accident has been taken place in the middle between last lane and the middle lane of the road.

Thus Ex-P4 clearly demonstrate that the accident had been taken place as the driver of the lorry i.e., respondent No.1 changed the lane from the middle of the lane without giving any signal and indicator.

Though the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet by holding that accused No.1 i.e., deceased was also driving the motor cycle in high speed and negligent manner and due to his negligence, he hit to the back side of the lorry.

But it is normal rule of the road that in the highway, every vehicle will be moving in the speed manner, mere the deceased was driving the bike in speed itself does not amount to the rash and negligence.

As in the present case, if at at all the driver of the lorry i.e.,
respondent No.1 would not have changed the lane without giving any indicator or signal, no accident would have taken place.
Thus it clearly shows that accident had been taken place due to sole negligence of the driver of the lorry itself.

There is a rule of road that in a national highway before changing the lane, the driver of the vehicle must giving indictor and signal and thereafter after looking into the vehicles coming from the back side on the other lane, the driver has to change the lane.

Even the pillion rider who is a material witness to the accident has clearly deposed and stated in his evidence that on that day when he and the deceased Naveen Rajur were going on the bike, at that time, the lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-5136 was going in front of their motor cycle and without giving any signal turn or indicator immediately slow down and turn the lorry and due to the Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/
5 negligence back side of the lorry dashed against the motor cycle and it is pertinent to not here that this fact has not been denied by the learned counsel for the respondent at least by putting single suggestion.

The learned counsel for the respondent only made suggestion that accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the Naveen Rajur and said suggestion was outrightly denied by the PW-2.
Though respondent counsel argued and contended that due to sole negligence of the deceased, accident had been taken place and there is no negligence on the part of the respondent No.1.
But respondent No.1 counsel not at all examined the driver of the lorry and disprove the evidence of the PW-1 and PW-2.

The respondent No.1 Praveen is a material eye witness as to state under what circumstances, the accident had been taken place, but respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and given the evidence and subjected himself for the cross examination by the petitioner counsel.
Hence an adverse inference can be drawn against the respondent No.1 for not leading the evidence of the material witness.
Under such circumstances the evidence of the PW-2 is acceptable and believable.
Even it is not the case of defence of respondent No.1 that respondent No.1 never changed lane or has given indicator and signal before changing lane.
Under such facts and circumstances it can be held that due to rash and negligence of driver of lorry, respondent No.1 accident taken place.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 & PW-2 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 and 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

15. The unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the driver of offending lorry and in the said accident Naveen Rajur (in MVC No.3813/2021) died and petitioner( in MVC No.3814/2021) sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
16. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 and 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 and 2 in both cases is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
18. Issue No.3 and 4 in MVC No. 3813/2021 :
The petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of his chief- examination and deposed that she is the mother.
The petitioner has produced Ex-P9-ration card and Ex-P10 and 11- adhar cards and from the said ration card and adhaar cards, it reveals that petitioner is the mother of the deceased Naveen Rajur.

Therefore I can safely hold that the said petitioner is the the legal representatives of the deceased and she is entitle for compensation under the following heads :
19. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS : In the Aadhaar card (Ex.P11) the date of birth of deceased is reflected as 15-7-2000.
This indicates that deceased was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 15 to 20 is '18'.
this fact has not been disputed by the respondent.

Though petitioner stated that deceased Naveen Rajur was working as a agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., The petitioners have not produced any document regarding avocation and income of deceased Naveen Rajur.
In the absence of proof, this Court has to consider the income notionally for calculating the compensation.

As the accident took place in the year 2021, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m. by taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.

20. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 20 years.
21. As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157, 40% of income is to be added towards future prospects in case of self employed.
40% of Rs.15000/- works out to Rs.6000/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.21000/- (15000+6000).

Admittedly, the deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.21,000/- works out to Rs.10,500/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.10500/- (21000- 10500).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,26,000/- (10500 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '18'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.22,68,000/- (1,26,000 X 18).
22. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/
7 others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/-

sentences.text:
(in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of filial consortium and loss of love & affection.
23. LOSS OF ESTATE:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
24. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

25. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency 22,68,000 2 Loss of Consortium 48,400 3 Loss of Estate 18,150 4 Funeral Expenses 18,150 Total 23,52,700 Hence, petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.23,52,700/-.
26. Issue No.3 in MVC No. 3814/2021 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-5136.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
27. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 21 years.
The petitioner has produced the Ex-P.18-Aadhaar card which reveals petitioner's year of birth is 19-11-1999 and as on the date of accident, petitioner was aged about 21 years, six months, ten days.
The petitioner has stated that he was an agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding is avocation and income.
28. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-

In order to prove his injuries, petitioner got examined himself as PW-2 and Dr.K.M.Kumaraswamy as PW-4. PW-2 in MVC No.3814/23 has stated that he sustained injuries i.e., bilateral hebork II fracture of maxia and patela bone split mid joint and symphosis fracture of mandible and degloving fracture of tooth and head injury bilateral fracture undisplaced maxillary.

But in the cross-examination PW-4 clearly admitted that in the wound certificate it is clearly stated that the petitioner has sustained simple injuries and the injuries mentioned in para No.1 of his affidavit i.e., degloving fracture of tooth has not been mentioned in discharge summary.
Even further PW-4 admitted that in the discharge summary degloving fracture has not been mentioned.
Further PW-4 pleaded his ignorance about what are all the complaints and the injuries stated by the petitioner in his evidence.

Further PW-4 stated that as per the say of the petitioner, he has mentioned about those problems in Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/
8
his affidavit
. Further even PW-4 admitted that there is no medical records to show that petitioner had sustained missing of teeth.
PW-4 stated that as per the say of the petitioner, he stated that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, petitioner has lost his teeth.
Further even PW-2 admitted that he has not verified any of the medical records with regard to the treatment taken by the petitioner between 10- 6-2021 to 7-12-2023.

PW-4 doctor has given the disability of 10% to the missing teeth and 5%
for mobility of the teeth and 5% for mal-union present in the mandible and for the whole- body disability at 20%.
29.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
30.
Looking into the nature and gravity of the findings, petitioner has sustained loss of tooth and there is mal-union present in the mandible i.e., lower jaw.
All these injuries will not in any way hamper functional capacity of the petitioner.
Hence, this court is of the opinion that petitioner has not sustained any functional disability due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

Therefore,
petitioner is not entitle any compensation under this head.

31. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e.,Ex-P15-wound certificate (1) laceration over both upper and lower hips (2)
laceration over right eyelid with globe injury (3) crush injury to face with facial bones injury and the doctor has opined that the injuries No.1 to 3 are simple in nature.
Ex-P12-discharge summary of Mangala Multi speciality hospital, Hassan, peititoner has sustained injuries i.e., bilateral hebork II fracture of maxia and patela bone split mid joint and symphosis fracture of mandible and degloving fracture of tooth and head injury bilateral fracture undisplaced maxillary and for which petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 30- 5-2021 to 10-6-2021 i.e., for 11 days.
The petitioner has stated that he is suffering with permanent disablement and deformity to attend his work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 21 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- under this head.

32. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 11 days as inpatient, it is quite natural Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/
9 that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 2 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.30,000/- (15,000 X 2) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.

33. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Alur Taluk, Hassan district and has taken treatment as inpatient at Mangala Multi speciality hospital, Hassan and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 11 days and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

34. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.75,000/- is awarded under this head.
35. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical bills Ex-P13 and medical prescriptions Ex- P14 for Rs.1,81,000/-.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.1,81,000/-
under the head of medical expenses.

36. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Pain & sufferings :
Rs.2,00,000/-
2 Loss of income during : Rs. 30,000/-
laid-up period 3

Attendant charges, extra : Rs. 30,000/-
 nutritious food &
 conveyance charges  4 Loss of future amenities : Rs. 75,000/-
 & happiness Dileepa Y.P vs Praveen.R on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104662700/
10

5 Medical expenses : Rs. 1,81,000/-
 Total Rs.5,16,000/-
Hence petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.5,16,000/-.

37. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

38. The respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.3 in MVC No.3814/2021 and issue No.4 in MVC No.3813/2021 are answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
39.
ISSUE NO.4 in MVC No.3814/2021 and ISSUE No.5 in MVC No.3813/2021

: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petitions filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, are hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms:
The petitioner in MVC No.3813/2021 is entitle for compensation of Rs.23,52,700/-
and petitioner in MVC No.3814/2021 is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,16,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

opennyai_summary.arguments: The tribunal even otherwise is under statutory obligation under rule 235 of Karnataka motor vehicles Rules 1989 to send notice to owner/s and driver/s of the vehicles said to have been involved in an accident and call upon them to produce any evidence they may wish to tender on issue of negligence and as held by Apex court in case of Machindranath Kernath Kasar Vs D.S.Mylarappa and Ors on 29/4/2008(2008 ACJ page 1964) wherein it is held that driver is a necessary party to decide issue of negligence.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet by holding that accused No.1 i.e., deceased was also driving the motor cycle in high speed and negligent manner and due to his negligence, he hit to the back side of the lorry.
But it is normal rule of the road that in the highway, every vehicle will be moving in the speed manner, mere the deceased was driving the bike in speed itself does not amount to the rash and negligence.
As in the present case, if at at all the driver of the lorry i.e.,
respondent No.1 would not have changed the lane without giving any indicator or signal, no accident would have taken place.
Thus it clearly shows that accident had been taken place due to sole negligence of the driver of the lorry itself.
There is a rule of road that in a national highway before changing the lane, the driver of the vehicle must giving indictor and signal and thereafter after looking into the vehicles coming from the back side on the other lane, the driver has to change the lane.
Hence an adverse inference can be drawn against the respondent No.1 for not leading the evidence of the material witness.
Under such circumstances the evidence of the PW-2 is acceptable and believable.
Even it is not the case of defence of respondent No.1 that respondent No.1 never changed lane or has given indicator and signal before changing lane.
Under such facts and circumstances it can be held that due to rash and negligence of driver of lorry, respondent No.1 accident taken place.
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 & PW-2 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 and 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 and 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
20. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
30.
Looking into the nature and gravity of the findings, petitioner has sustained loss of tooth and there is mal-union present in the mandible i.e., lower jaw.
All these injuries will not in any way hamper functional capacity of the petitioner.
Hence, this court is of the opinion that petitioner has not sustained any functional disability due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Therefore,
petitioner is not entitle any compensation under this head.
